en_plurals.says: 'Oxen', 'children' and 'brethren' are the plurals of 'ox', 'child' and 'brother'; they are English nouns, not archaic, dialect or jocular forms.

three_only.says: Leaving aside archaic, dialect and jocular forms, the English plurals in '-en' are 'oxen', 'children' and 'brethren'. (stored closed list)
three_only.z3: ForAll(n, Implies(And(english_noun(n), Not(archaic_or_jocular(n)), endswith(plural_form(n), "en")), Or(n == "ox", n == "child", n == "brother")))

oxen_only.says: 'Oxen' is the only plain '-en' plural: 'children' adds '-ren' and 'brethren' changes the vowel. (stored closed list)
oxen_only.z3: ForAll(n, Implies(And(english_noun(n), Not(archaic_or_jocular(n)), plural_form(n) == n + "en"), n == "ox"))
